title: Advent Lanterns
subject: Contracts
stem:
Preparing for a fall youth-ministry expo, Lydia Supply, a private retreat-supply reseller, sent Barnabas Crafts a purchase order for 1,200 battery-powered Advent lantern kits. Barnabas received the order by courier on May 6. The form called for delivery no earlier than August 20 and no later than September 10, but a bold box above the signature line read: “Lydia Supply reserves the right to cancel this order at any time before August 12.” On May 8, Barnabas mailed Lydia Supply a signed reply stating, “We accept your order,” and Lydia Supply received it on May 9.

As of May 10, which statement is accurate as to whether a contract was formed?
call: As of May 10, which statement is accurate as to whether a contract was formed?

choices.A: No contract was formed, because Lydia Supply’s purchase order was merely a revocable offer.
choices.B: A contract was formed, but before August 12 it was an option contract cancelable only at Lydia Supply’s election.
choices.C: No contract was formed, because Lydia Supply reserved the right to cancel the order.
choices.D: A contract was formed, but before August 12 it was terminable at the election of either party.

rightExplanation:
C is correct. Lydia Supply did not merely state a delivery schedule or reserve an ordinary remedy. It reserved the right to cancel the order at any time before August 12, before performance was due. That means Lydia Supply had not made a real commitment to buy the lantern kits as of May 10.

Gold Key: A buyer’s apparent promise is illusory when the buyer reserves an unrestricted right to cancel before it must perform; the seller’s acceptance does not convert that escape hatch into an option contract.

Silver Key: Decide formation before labels. The answer set tries to pull the student into “revocable offer” and “option contract” labels, but the first question is whether the cancellation reservation leaves any binding buyer promise.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: A talks about the order being revocable. The stem gives an acceptance and no cancellation. Cut as NOT_RESPONSIVE / wrong_element.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: D gives the cancellation power to either party. The stem gives it only to Lydia Supply. Cut as NOT_TRUE / flat_misstatement.

c3.label: CLASH C vs B
c3.text: Both notice Lydia Supply’s unilateral cancellation power. The axis is: Does that power mean no contract, or does it create a formed option-style contract?

c3.label: CALL with Gold Key
c3.text: The cancellation power makes Lydia Supply’s promise illusory before performance. That resolves the residue to C.

studentScript: Formation first. The seller accepted, so do not stop at revocable offer. But the buyer kept the right to cancel before it had to perform, so the buyer’s promise is illusory. Pick C.

A.signal: The choice points to pre-acceptance revocability, but the stem gives acceptance and no cancellation.
A.lawyer: A revocable offer can still become a contract if accepted before revocation; this answer misses the illusory-promise issue.

B.signal: The choice reaches for a familiar label after seeing one-sided cancellation.
B.lawyer: The unilateral cancellation reservation creates an illusory-promise problem, not an option contract.

C.signal: It matches the cancellation-reservation trigger and answers formation.
C.lawyer: The unrestricted cancellation right makes Lydia Supply’s promise illusory as of May 10.

D.signal: The cancellation right belongs only to Lydia Supply.
D.lawyer: No reciprocal termination right was stated for Barnabas.

goldKeys.statement: A buyer's apparent promise is illusory when the buyer reserves an unrestricted right to cancel before it must perform; the seller's acceptance does not convert that escape hatch into an option contract.
goldKeys.trigger: A purchase order or acceptance set says one side may cancel at any time before the date performance is due.
goldKeys.unlocks: Distinguishes no contract from the dominant option-contract trap.
goldKeys.authority: UCC §1-103(b); Restatement (Second) of Contracts §77; UCC §§2-204, 2-206, and 2-205 for the formation and firm-offer contrast.

silverKeys.statement: When the answer set splits between 'no contract' and 'contract formed with a label,' decide formation before choosing the label. A familiar label cannot save a formed-contract answer if the cancellation power means one side has not made a real commitment.
silverKeys.trigger: Two choices say no contract; two choices say contract formed but fight over who may cancel.

remediation.title: One-sided cancellation before performance
remediation.signal: A purchase order says one side may cancel at any time before the performance window.
remediation.studentMove: Do not label it as an option first; ask whether that party made a real commitment.
remediation.tinyRule: Unrestricted cancellation before performance makes that side’s promise illusory.
remediation.trap: Treating the one-sided escape hatch as a formed option contract.
